A.explanation: Wrong side and wrong angle. East of north would add to the eastward wind drift, and $23.0^{\circ}$ comes from using $\tan\theta = 85.0/200$ instead of sine.

B.explanation: Correct side to oppose the wind but wrong angle. $23.0^{\circ}$ is $\tan^{-1}(85.0/200)$, which treats $200 \text{ km h}^{-1}$ as the adjacent side rather than the hypotenuse.

C.explanation: Correct magnitude of $25.2^{\circ}$ but wrong side. Steering east of north gives an eastward component that adds to the $85.0 \text{ km h}^{-1}$ wind blowing toward the east.

D.explanation: Steering west of north provides a westward component to cancel the eastward wind, with $\sin\theta = 85.0/200$ giving $\theta = 25.2^{\circ}$.

hints: Notice the wind blows from the west, so its velocity vector points toward the east at $85.0 \text{ km h}^{-1}$ and must be cancelled for resultant motion due north.
Draw the velocity triangle with the $200 \text{ km h}^{-1}$ aircraft heading as the hypotenuse and the due-north resultant as one side, so the westward heading component balances the eastward wind.
Relate the angle west of north to opposite over hypotenuse: $\sin\theta = 85.0/200$, and check why $\tan^{-1}(85.0/200) = 23.0^{\circ}$ is not correct here.
walkthrough: Wind from the west means air moves from west to east. So the wind velocity is $85.0 \text{ km h}^{-1}$ toward the east and will push a northbound aircraft eastward.

To fly due north, the vector sum of aircraft velocity relative to air plus wind velocity must point due north. The aircraft must therefore aim partly west to give a westward component that cancels the eastward wind.

Draw a right-angled vector triangle: hypotenuse is the aircraft speed in still air, $200 \text{ km h}^{-1}$, angled $\theta$ west of north; east-west components must balance, north-south side is the resultant ground track due north.

In the east-west direction: $200 \sin\theta = 85.0$, with speeds in $\text{km h}^{-1}$. This uses sine because $200 \text{ km h}^{-1}$ is the hypotenuse and $85.0 \text{ km h}^{-1}$ is the side opposite $\theta$.
The required heading is therefore $25.2^{\circ}$ to the west of north to cancel the eastward push. This is option D.
